extraction.paper_title: A Spectral Approach to Scalable Vectorless Thermal Integrity Verification

scenario.figure_or_table: Table I (Statistics of two microprocessor designs) with Table II (results for test cases T1-T7) and Figures 3-4 (worst-case temperature distributions)
scenario.description: Vectorless worst-case thermal integrity verification of two microprocessor designs, Processor A and Processor B (designs taken from Li et al. [8]). The paper gives only total power, die area, layer counts, and equivalent heat transfer coefficients, with no block-level floorplan geometry or per-block power. Power is treated as local and global constraints (bounds), not fixed values. Processor A is the identified scenario: 28 W, 195 mm2, 4 metal layers, 11 material layers, 3.3e3 W/m2K for the heat sink and 2.0e3 W/m2K for the package.
scenario.architecture: Processor A: 3D multilayer thermal grid with 11 material layers and 4 metal layers, die area 195 mm2, heat sink coefficient 3.3e3 W/m2K, package coefficient 2.0e3 W/m2K. Processor B (6 metal layers, 15 material layers, 302 mm2, 50 W) is the second design and is not selected.
scenario.workload: Vectorless uncertain power-density workloads defined by local bounds (bL <= b <= bU) and global block bounds (BL <= Mb <= BU). Exact bounds are not given in the packet. Total power is 28 W for Processor A.
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state worst-case temperature search over 3D thermal grids (Table II grid sizes 25K to 2.0M nodes). Ambient temperature and absolute temperature values are not stated; the figures show node-indexed temperature distributions. Solver: Cholesky (CHOLMOD) plus Gurobi LP, with spectral sparsification, edge scaling, multilevel AMG, and weighted Jacobi refinement.

original_setup.solver: Steady-state 3D thermal grid solve T x = b with CHOLMOD Cholesky factorization, plus spectral graph sparsification, iterative edge weight scaling, AMG-based multilevel coarsening and weighted Jacobi solution refinement (MATLAB and C++). Selected scenario: Processor A.
original_setup.optimizer: Gurobi LP solver for vectorless worst-case power vector search under local (bL<=b<=bU) and global (BL<=Mb<=BU) power constraints
original_setup.controller: None. This is a steady-state verification method with no runtime thermal controller or DTM.
original_setup.benchmark: Processor A (28 W, 195 mm2, 4 metal layers, 11 material layers, heat sink 3.3e3 W/m2K, package 2.0e3 W/m2K) from Li et al. [8]; Table II test cases T1-T7 (25K to 2.0M nodes); worst-case temperature distributions in Fig. 3 (Processor A).

thermal_observable.location: Per node of the 3D thermal grid; worst-case temperature distribution (node-indexed) for Processor A, Fig. 3. No numeric temperatures, units or ambient value are stated in the text.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Worst-case (maximum) temperature per node t_i = e_i^T T^-1 b, maximized by LP over local and global power constraints, giving twst = T^-1 bwst. Runtimes in Table II are summed over 100 randomly chosen nodes.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper gives no block-level floorplan (no x, y, width or height) and no per-block power for Processor A. Only total power (28 W), die area, layer counts and heat transfer coefficients are given on page 5, Table I. Total power must not be split without a published rule, so no complete floorplan experiment can be built.

Power is a set of uncertain local and global bounds, not fixed per-block watts. The observable is an LP-derived worst-case temperature over a power-vector set, not a temperature for a single deterministic power assignment, so it cannot be reproduced by a single-power-map Studio run.

The original model is a multilayer 3D thermal grid (11 material layers, 4 metal layers) with equivalent heat-transfer-coefficient boundaries for heat sink and package. It is not a 2D steady floorplan model, and the layer thicknesses and materials are not given in the packet.

The original solver and optimizer stack (spectral sparsification, multilevel AMG, weighted Jacobi refinement, Gurobi LP) differs from any bundled Studio solver. The paper reports runtime and approximation error and does not report absolute temperatures.

There is no transient, controller, interposer or reliability modelling. Reliability is only motivated qualitatively. These are not mismatches that affect a steady-state setup, but no corresponding data exist.

methods.note: Pages 2-4 support the extracted method description: steady-state T x = b, LP with local and global constraints (Eq. 2-3), spectral sparsification, edge scaling (Alg. 1), Jacobi refinement (Alg. 2), and the multilevel AMG flow (Alg. 3). Page 5 supports CHOLMOD and Gurobi, MATLAB and C++, and the 2.67 GHz CPU. The method is correctly marked as 3D, vectorless and LP-based, not a 2D reproduction. This verifies the method description only, not any reproducible experiment.

code.note: The packet has no assets and no linked code or repository (artifact_search_status checked_no_links). The only external pointers are citations to CHOLMOD and Gurobi. A URL or citation is not evidence of runnable code. No implementation is available.

parameters.note: Table I values for Processor A are supported on page 5: 28 W, 195 mm2, 4 metal layers, 11 material layers, 3.3 and 2.0 (x10^3 W/m2K). The 195 mm2 to 1.95e-4 m2 and 10^3 coefficient conversions are arithmetically correct. The algorithm parameters are not extracted and are not given in the text: epsilon, k, gamma, Nmax, beta, eps_th and the gmin value. The power bounds, the matrix M, the layer thicknesses and conductivities, and the ambient temperature are also absent. Because several decisive parameters are unavailable, this is not resolved.

config.note: No floorplan geometry, block names, per-block power, local or global constraint values, 3D grid dimensions, or test-case-to-processor mapping exists in the PDF text. The experiment is empty (floorplan [] and power_w {}), so no same-scenario power exists for any floorplan block. The record is also internally inconsistent: experiment.kind is custom_2d_steady while steady_2d_relevant is false and the model is 3D multilayer.

data.note: The decisive observable is the node-indexed worst-case temperature distribution in Fig. 3 (page 6). Only pdftotext output was supplied, so the figure was not visually verified or digitized and has no numeric values. Table II is text-extracted only and is not tied to Processor A. The packet has no data assets. The Table I coefficient row is column-merged in the extraction, so the shared-value reading is an inference from layout.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The deterministic gate failed on input validity: a custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object, but the extraction supplies an empty floorplan and no power map. The scenario is Processor A from Li et al. (28 W, 195 mm2, 4 metal and 11 material layers, heat sink 3.3e3 and package 2.0e3 W/m2K) from a vectorless worst-case thermal integrity paper. Its observable is an LP-derived worst-case node temperature over bounded local/global power sets on a 3D multilayer grid. No numeric temperature, unit or ambient value is extractable, so the paper gives only a node-indexed distribution in Fig. 3. Because no Studio result exists, there is no Studio temperature to compare, and comparison_valid is false. No numerical comparison is made, and no replication, agreement or disagreement is claimed. Even if a run were possible, a custom 2D steady run would have no transient trace and would not match the paper's vectorless worst-case LP observable, 3D grid, or solver stack. Only the qualitative point stands: the paper's method is about how uncertain power bounds drive worst-case temperature, but this cannot be tested here. The gate also lists unresolved evidence locators and adversarial/independent review checks, so the extracted inputs are not verified.
limitations: Studio was skipped; there are no simulation outputs or artifacts to assess, and comparison_valid is false.

No linked code, data or configuration assets were found, and the gate reports unresolved evidence locator, adversarial and independent review checks, so independent verification is absent.
